ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given: As shown in the figure, segment $AB=6\text{cm}$, point $P$ is a moving point on segment $AB$, with sides $AP$, $BP$ to construct equilateral $\triangle APC$ and equilateral $\triangle BPD$ respectively on $AB$, connect $CD$, point $M$ is the midpoint of $CD$. When point $P$ moves from point $A$ to point $B$, what is the length of the path traced by point $M$ in centimeters?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, extend AC and BD to meet at H. Through point M, draw GN $\parallel$ AB intersecting AH at G and BH at N,\\
$\because$ $\triangle APC$ and $\triangle BPD$ are both equilateral triangles,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle A=\angle B=\angle DPB=\angle CPA=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ AH $\parallel$ PD and BH $\parallel$ CP,\\
$\therefore$ quadrilateral CPDH is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore$ CD and HP bisect each other,\\
$\therefore$ M is the midpoint of PH,\\
Thus, as P moves, M always remains at the midpoint of HP, so the trajectory of M is indeed the median of $\triangle HAB$, that is, the segment GN,\\
$\therefore$ $GN=\frac{1}{2}AB=\boxed{3}$ cm.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A, P, B are on the same horizontal line segment, and P is located between A and B; construct equilateral triangle APC above AP, with vertex C above the baseline AB; construct equilateral triangle BPD above PB, with vertex D above the baseline AB; connect C and D, and point M is marked on CD and indicated as the midpoint of CD. Reasoning: According to the coordinate method, let AB be the horizontal axis. Let A=(0,0), B=(6,0), P=(t,0), where 0≤t≤6. Because △APC is an equilateral triangle with AP as a side and above AB, C=(t/2, √3 t/2). Because △BPD is an equilateral triangle with PB as a side and above AB, D=((t+6)/2, √3(6-t)/2). Point M is the midpoint of CD, therefore the coordinates of M are: x_M = [t/2 + (t+6)/2]/2 = (t+3)/2, y_M = [√3 t/2 + √3(6-t)/2]/2 = 3√3/2. It can be seen that the vertical coordinate of M is constant, and the horizontal coordinate changes from 3/2 to 9/2 as t goes from 0 to 6, so the locus of M is a horizontal line segment, with length 9/2 - 3/2 = 3 cm.
